messages:
Emma: Hey team — I've uploaded a first-pass benchmark narrative + three chart mockups to the drive: https://rwd.internal/bench-draft. Goal is a short blog + 20-min webinar. Main story: show how batching + KV caching shifts the latency/cost frontier for common chat workloads. Feedback welcome, esp on which chart to lead with. 
Marta: skimmed — nice start. Quick data note: our p50 numbers look tight but p95 divergence is the headline risk. I ran a small sweep, TL;DR: batching reduces cost ~30% at p50, but p95 tail stays ~1.5-2x unless we enable prefix caching. 
Marta: paste of helper table I used:
```
workload,type,p50_ms,p95_ms,cost_per_1k
chat-small,no-cache,45,220,$0.12
chat-small,batch-32,38,190,$0.085
chat-small,batch-32+cache,35,95,$0.06
long-context,no-cache,120,780,$0.45
long-context,batch-16,110,640,$0.33
long-context,batch-16+cache,90,210,$0.20
```
Raj: This is great. For messaging, suggest two parallel frames: 1) Economics — show dollars/token with simple percent delta bars. 2) Reliability — show p95 tail improvement when cache is on. Lead slide should be single stat + visual (e.g., "Up to 60% lower token cost + 3x tail reduction"). Avoid model names in the headline, keep it workload-focused. 
Liam: design notes — the mockups look busy. If we lead with the percent delta stat, use a horizontal waterfall chart for cost delta and a compact sparkline with p95 overlay for latency. Also prefer consistent color: green for cost improvement, amber for latency risk. I can whip these up if someone confirms the final numbers. 
Olivia: who is our target audience for the webinar? enterprise infra/platform teams or PLG engineers? We need to tailor the CTA — e.g., "try a tuned config" vs "book a Dedicated consult" will change the footer copy and the inbound routing. 
Emma: Good call. For the first webinar, aim at platform teams at scale (<-$2M ARR product teams and up). CTA = "Schedule a capacity review" + link to routing form that includes team size and security tier. Olivia can you draft the routing fields? 
Olivia: Yep. Draft routing fields: org size, primary use case (chat/embeddings/batch), compliance needs, preferred deployment (hosted/dedicated/private). Also add an optional upload for a sample prompt set — we'll queue those into the eval team. 
eng-bench-bot: benchmark run complete for sweep id=sw-2026-39. Artifacts: s3://bench/2026/sw-39/{summary.csv,plots.tar.gz}. p95 improvements when cache enabled: median 2.8x across chat-small runs. 
Marta: small ask — can we include an inset showing cost per successful response (i.e., end-to-end throughput adjusted for retries/timeouts)? That helps the reliability framing. I can compute if you give me the final sample rate and timeout policy. 
Raj: Agree on inset. Also, let's call out the assumptions clearly: model family, sequence length distribution, tokenization, and whether expensive ops (tool calls) are included. A callout box "Assumptions" on every chart. 
Liam: I'll make two variants: one marketing-friendly (clean, bold stat) and one technical appendix slide with the full tables. Which chart should go to the appendix? The long-context per-config table (it's dense). 
Emma: Appendix gets the heavy tables. Lead deck: 3 slides — 1) headline stat + simple cost delta, 2) p95 tail chart showing cache effect, 3) configuration checklist + CTA. Appendix: full tables and methodology. 
Olivia: Webinar promotion plan: short demo at minute 10 showing console routing + cost breakdown, live Q&A. We'll gate the demo by attendee size to keep it tight. Also route high-intent signups (org size >200, needs private) to sales. Low-intent to self-serve. 
Marta: final data point — for the blog post, include a small reproducible snippet showing how we measured tokens and cost in the SDK. Something like:
```
resp = client.generate(model='open-redwood-1', prompt=prompt)
print(resp.metrics.tokens_total, resp.metrics.cost_usd)
```
keeps it concrete. 
Emma: Love it. Action items: Marta finalize numbers + inset (due EOD tomorrow), Liam produce two slide variants (marketing + appendix) by Thursday, Olivia draft routing form and CTA copy by Thursday, Raj to review messaging and write the headline stat, Emma will assemble deck and draft blog intro. 
Raj: I'll take headline drafts. First pass: "Reduce inference token spend by up to 60% — keep latency predictable with config-level caching." Shorten/optimize tomorrow. 
Liam: tagging design review channel in case we need brand checks: <#design> :eyes: 
Olivia: I'll map the inbound routing to our CRM fields and mock the HubSpot form. Will add a hidden field for 'source=bench-webinar' for tracking. 
Emma: Thanks all. If nobody objects, I'll lock the narrative and we can rehearse next Tues. :thumbsup:
